purpose: Machine-readable record of every third-party container image and binary the product, the local audit, and the certification workflows depend on -- including the base images every Dockerfile FROMs, which is what lets a rebuild of a release commit produce the same bytes. backend/tests/test_third_party_image_lock.py fails the build if a reference site and this file disagree in either direction, if any Dockerfile FROMs an external image that is not locked here, if this file names an image nothing uses, if a compose service pulls a mutable tag, or if a locked digest is not the index digest the cited registry evidence measures. Digests are generated, not transcribed: scripts/release/third_party_registry_evidence.py resolves every coordinate this file names against its registry and writes the tracked artifact every entry points at.

minio_object_store.why: The upstream vendor archived the open-source MinIO Server, Client and KES and stopped serving community release files (see the note in docs/known-issues.md). A tag is a mutable pointer into a registry whose retention policy we do not control, and this image stores certified evidence, so the release line pins content by digest and re-derives the digest from the vendor's signed release tag before changing it.
minio_object_store.upgrade_procedure: 1) resolve the new tag at https://quay.io/v2/minio/minio/manifests/<tag> with an Accept header for the docker/oci manifest LIST (a bare request returns a legacy schema1 conversion whose digest differs); 2) confirm the image config labels carry release=<tag> and vendor=MinIO Inc; 3) confirm the matching PGP-signed tag in github.com/minio/minio was created minutes before the image build timestamp; 4) update this file, then run the object-store certification (pytest -m object_store + the Linux/GA workflows) before any release.

compose_images.why: A tag is a pointer the vendor moves. Every external image a compose deployment pulls is therefore pinned to the manifest-list digest the tracked registry evidence resolves, so a redeploy of a release commit cannot silently run different bytes than the ones that were certified. The index digest -- not the linux/amd64 child -- is what keeps a non-amd64 host pulling its own platform build.
compose_images.upgrade_procedure: 1) run scripts/release/third_party_registry_evidence.py and commit the regenerated docs/quality/artifacts/registry-resolution/third-party-registries.json; 2) review the digest diff it produced -- a moved tag and a deliberate version bump look the same here and are not the same decision; 3) re-run the certification that covers the images that moved; 4) only then update docker-compose.yml and this file in one commit, because the reference-site test fails between the two halves.

postgres.why: This entry used to record `tag` on the stated grounds that postgres:16-alpine is a Docker Hub official-library image whose tag is maintained upstream. The reason it was really tag-pinned was that no digest could be resolved from the audit host while Docker Hub was unreachable from it -- a transport fact about one machine, not an argument for mutable deployment. The generator now resolves the index digest and round-trips it by digest, so this file carries the digest like every other compose image.
postgres.upgrade_procedure: 1) scripts/release/third_party_registry_evidence.py, commit the regenerated artifact; 2) review the digest diff, since moving a digest here also stops upstream patch flow for the pinned surfaces; 3) re-run the PostgreSQL version matrix (section 6 of the release checklist) -- it certifies Debian-suffix variants, not this alpine digest, so a pin bump is where that gap is paid back; 4) update this file together with every surface in `referenced_by`.
postgres.known_cost: Pinning `16-alpine` means a compose deployment no longer receives Docker Hub's patch rebuilds of that tag until someone performs the upgrade procedure above.

binaries.role: the Docker CLI build plugin the release builds run under
binaries.install_contract: docker/setup-buildx-action installs it from this release; the pinned action SHA and the explicit buildx-version input together decide which binary lands on the runner
binaries.why_not_latest: setup-buildx-action without buildx-version takes whatever the action's pinned commit considers current, so the CLI -- and with it the BuildKit daemon it starts -- changes when the action is bumped rather than when this file says so
